champion: Meperidine-Induced Skin and Soft Tissue Injury
ordered_diagnoses: Meperidine-Induced Skin and Soft Tissue Injury

facts.raw_span: 7-year history of severe, mechanical, low back pain
long-standing mental depression
self-administering subcutaneous injections of meperidine, 100 mg 4 times per day, for the past 3 years
Large and deep, irregularly shaped, cutaneous ulcer on the dorsum of right forearm with necrotic tissue and muscle exposure at the base
Woody induration of skin on both forearms and abdominal region
Bilateral contracture of deltoid, triceps, and biceps muscles
Active and passive range of motion restricted at shoulders and elbows
No signs of joint inflammation
Elevated serum creatinine kinase (192 U/L; reference range, 0-174 U/L)
Normal complete blood cell count
Shows lobular panniculitis, subcutaneous fat lobules with necrotic adipocytes and dense inflammatory infiltrates composed mainly of foamy histiocytes
Deltoid muscle biopsy showed no muscle involvement

concepts.why: The patient's history of self-administering subcutaneous injections of meperidine, combined with the presence of large and deep cutaneous ulcers, woody induration of skin, and histopathology showing lobular panniculitis, supports the diagnosis of necrotizing panniculitis.

concepts.preferred_label: Meperidine-Induced Skin and Soft Tissue Injury
concepts.why: The patient's history of self-administering subcutaneous injections of meperidine, combined with the presence of large and deep cutaneous ulcers and woody induration of skin, supports the diagnosis of meperidine-induced skin and soft tissue injury.

aliases: Bilateral Contracture of Deltoid, Triceps, and Biceps Muscles
concepts.why: The patient's history of self-administering subcutaneous injections of meperidine, combined with the presence of bilateral contracture of deltoid, triceps, and biceps muscles, supports the diagnosis of contracture of the upper limb.
The patient's laboratory test results showing elevated serum creatinine kinase support the diagnosis of elevated creatine kinase.

aliases: Subcutaneous Fat Lobules with Necrotic Adipocytes
concepts.why: The patient's histopathology results showing lobular panniculitis support the diagnosis of lobular panniculitis.
The patient's history of self-administering subcutaneous injections of meperidine supports the diagnosis of meperidine abuse.
The patient's history of severe, mechanical, low back pain and long-standing mental depression supports the diagnosis of chronic pain syndrome.
The patient's history of bilateral contracture of deltoid, triceps, and biceps muscles supports the diagnosis of muscle fibrosis.

rationales.F03: Meperidine injections are a known cause of skin and soft tissue injury.
rationales.F04: The presence of a large and deep cutaneous ulcer is highly suggestive of necrotizing panniculitis.
rationales.F05: Woody induration of the skin is a characteristic feature of meperidine-induced skin and soft tissue injury.
rationales.F06: Bilateral contracture of the deltoid, triceps, and biceps muscles is a sign of chronic muscle fibrosis.
rationales.F09: Elevated serum creatinine kinase is a marker of muscle damage.
rationales.F11: Lobular panniculitis is a characteristic histopathological feature of necrotizing panniculitis.
rationales.F12: The absence of muscle involvement in the deltoid muscle biopsy rules out muscle fibrosis as a primary diagnosis.
